banner.title: THE DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 26-27, R546: printed pp. 95-96 (pdf 96-97) - the individual area key crosses the dead ground and the crowded maze: Area 26 the Hallowed Grounds (the multitude of natural caverns holding some of the largest chambers in all Deepearth - ceilings 1,000 feet or more, caverns over a mile wide and a dozen miles long, floors cut by bridged gorges, side tunnels, ruins and fortifications; the streams and small deep lakes; the barren beaten look with broken formations and collapsed bridges; the battle debris of broken weapons, shattered war machines and thousands upon thousands of skeletons - drow, duergar, svirfneblin, derro, plus the skeleton-less pech, cloakers and illithids who also fought and died; the sacrosanct spirits rising as wights, wraiths, spectres, ghosts and skeletons to marshall against trespassers, each huge cavern commanded by a single lich; the plentiful air and water but no food; the centuries-scavenged battlefields; and the treasure houses - city or fortification ruins holding thousands of weapons, mundane armor and war machines, fortunes in coins, gems and jewelry, and battle magic - weapons, armor, scrolls, rings, potions, wands, rods and miscellaneous items beyond measure - each guarded by an undead army commanded by a lich of 18-27th level (17 + 1d10), twenty percent of the liches magic user/clerics and the other 80% magic-users only), and Area 27 the Melting Pot (the contrast realm of many small caverns in an intricate maze of natural and artificial tunnels, amply watered with lustrous formations; the dwellings of most intelligent creatures known to Deepearth - drow, duergar, pech, derro, cloakers, myconids, umber hulks, even kuo-toa - each race in a 1d12-cave niche, vigorously defended with fortified construction, traps and war training; the rothe herds and edible fungus plots; the sacred unpollutable water sources; the nearly exhausted mineral veins and the wise use of raw materials; and the long-history secret passages and concealed entrances giving many possible routes between locations).

banner.sentinel: A procedural-plus-prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the ceiling minimum, the lich level bounds and the 17+1d10 dice-sides-base triple, the lich caste percentage, and the 1d12 niche dice-sides pair. The geography, denizens, resources and unique-features prose pins as bools for both areas. The undead/MM/magic-item/mining seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnaoCeilMinFt
consts.comment: soaring ceilings reach 1,000 feet or more above the floors.

consts.name: dnaoLichLvlMin
consts.comment: each treasure house army is commanded by a lich of 18-27th level (the low bound).

consts.name: dnaoLichLvlMax
consts.comment: the commanding liches range up to 27th level (the high bound).

consts.name: dnaoLichLvlDice
consts.comment: the lich level is 17 + 1d10 (the die count).

consts.name: dnaoLichLvlSides
consts.comment: the lich level is 17 + 1d10 (the die sides).

consts.name: dnaoLichDualPct
consts.comment: twenty percent of the liches are magic user/clerics and the other 80% are only magic-users.

consts.name: dnaoNicheDice
consts.comment: each race has secured a small niche of 1d12 caves (the die count).

consts.name: dnaoNicheSides
consts.comment: each racial niche is 1d12 caves (the die sides).

bools.name: dnaoVastCaverns
bools.comment: this multitude of natural caverns includes some of the largest chambers in all of Deepearth, with numerous excavated side tunnels and places showing fortifications and the ruins of large cities.

bools.name: dnaoMileWideChambers
bools.comment: caverns over a mile wide and a dozen miles long are common.

bools.name: dnaoGorgeBridges
bools.comment: many cavern floors are cut by deep, wide gorges, several of which have been bridged.

bools.name: dnaoStreamsLakes
bools.comment: several streams provide the area's water supply and some caverns contain small, deep lakes.

bools.name: dnaoBarrenBeaten
bools.comment: the caves once held many elegant formations but now have a barren and beaten look - stalactites and stalagmites broken, many bridges collapsed.

bools.name: dnaoBattleDebris
bools.comment: the debris of battle lies everywhere: broken weapons, shattered war machines, and thousands upon thousands of skeletons.

bools.name: dnaoNothingLives
bools.comment: nothing lives here anymore, though the caverns were once highly prized; the skeletons include drow, duergar, svirfneblin and derro, and the skeleton-less pech, cloakers and illithids also fought and died for control of these caverns.

bools.name: dnaoSpiritLegions
bools.comment: the spirits of the fallen warriors wish their battlegrounds to remain sacrosanct and rise up against trespassers: wights, wraiths, spectres, ghosts and skeletons marshall their forces to attack.

bools.name: dnaoLichPerCavern
bools.comment: each of the huge caverns contains a single lich that commands the many undead.

bools.name: dnaoNoFood
bools.comment: air and water are plentiful, but food is unavailable unless characters carry it with them.

bools.name: dnaoScavengedFields
bools.comment: each lich presides over a collection of valuables harvested from the battlefields by its undead minions over centuries; characters searching the battlefields find nothing but broken weapons, useless armor and other wreckage.

bools.name: dnaoTreasureHouses
bools.comment: each lich has selected the ruin of a once-vast city or fortification as its lair and treasure house, each holding thousands of normal weapons, mundane armor pieces and even war machines, plus a small fortune in coins, gems and jewelry plucked from the dead.

bools.name: dnaoBattleMagic
bools.comment: each treasure house contains a wide variety of magical items useful in battle - weapons, armor, scrolls, rings, potions, wands, rods and miscellaneous items beyond measure - guarded by a veritable army of undead.

bools.name: dnaoSmallCavernMaze
bools.comment: in contrast to the neighboring area, this realm features many small caverns connected by an intricate maze of tunnels and caverns of both natural and artificial origin; the caves receive ample water and the many formations retain a great deal of lustre.

bools.name: dnaoEveryRace
bools.comment: the caverns provide dwellings for most types of intelligent creatures known to Deepearth - populations of drow, duergar, pech, derro, cloakers, myconids, umber hulks and even kuo-toa.

bools.name: dnaoVigorousDefense
bools.comment: necessity has insured that each group is prepared to vigorously pursue its own defense: most construction effort goes to strengthening defenses, constructing traps and training individuals for war.

bools.name: dnaoRotheFungus
bools.comment: many of these races keep herds of rothe and raise large plots of edible fungus for sustenance.

bools.name: dnaoSacredWater
bools.comment: all creatures of the area agree that water sources are sacred and cannot be polluted or poisoned in the cause of war.

bools.name: dnaoExhaustedVeins
bools.comment: many mineral resources were once available throughout this realm, but nearly all such veins have been exhausted; the creatures have learned to use wisely what raw materials they can find.

bools.name: dnaoSecretRoutes
bools.comment: the long crowded history has left its mark in secret passages and connecting tunnels: inhabitants tunnel around areas that get in their way, so there are many possible routes between locations, often masked behind secret or concealed entrances.

examples.note: the hallowed grounds: ceilings 1,000 feet or more.

examples.expr: m['dnaoLichLvlMin']() != 18 or m['dnaoLichLvlMax']() != 27 or m['dnaoLichLvlDice']() != 1 or m['dnaoLichLvlSides']() != 10 or m['dnaoLichLvlBase']() != 17

examples.note: the lich castes: 20% magic user/clerics, 80% magic-users only.
the melting pot: 1d12 caves per racial niche.
